supported_claims: The displayed chapter is numbered 1 and contains verses 1:1 through 1:7.
A learner can identify chapter and verse numbers without using a translation to define the canonical locator.
not_supported: Any interpretive claim about the meaning of the surah without a selected and reviewed tafsir.
Rights to bundle Quran Foundation translations, tafsir or audio.

supported_claims: Tanzil permits attributed verbatim use of its Arabic Quran text under its stated terms.
not_supported: Permission to alter the Arabic text or reuse a translation or recitation.

lecture_outline: Show the chapter identifier and seven verse locators, without reproducing an unlicensed translation.
Ask the learner to locate 1:1, 1:4 and 1:7 and distinguish verse numbering from interpretation.
Explain that meaning, recitation and translation require separately selected and reviewed sources.
curated_next_batch.remaining_gate: Canonical text checksum, edition/licence attribution, translation/tafsir selection and Quran editor review.

supported_claims: The verse refers disputes to Allah and the Messenger.
not_supported: A complete theory of jurisprudence, the authority of a particular school or a ruling on a modern dispute.

supported_claims: The verse says the Reminder was sent down to the Prophet so he would explain what was revealed to people.
not_supported: A full classification of hadith, tafsir, fiqh and individual opinion from this verse alone.

lecture_outline: Identify the exact Qur'anic references and avoid treating a translation as the Arabic text.
Introduce the labels Quran, Sunnah, tafsir, fiqh and opinion as a question to research, not as an already sourced hierarchy.
Defer detailed distinctions and hadith grading until a named methodology source and qualified scholar review are recorded.
curated_next_batch.remaining_gate: Select exact hadith-method source/edition and reviewed definitions for all five categories; Islamic and language review.
